message.abstract: <jats:p>Under the background of a high proportion of wind power integration into the power grid, the wind power output exhibits significant volatility and time-variability at ultra-short-term scales, which poses challenges for real-time grid scheduling and safe operation. Existing short-horizon wind power forecasting methods struggle to effectively capture the dynamic characteristics of the spatial correlations among wind turbines within wind farms, which vary with wind conditions and operational states, limiting the forecasting accuracy and model adaptability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed dynamic spatiotemporal coupling method for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting (DSTC-Net). This method integrates multiple physical factors to construct a time-varying spatial correlation structure, and combines time-series modeling with an adaptive feature fusion mechanism to achieve collaborative modeling of dynamic spatial interactions among turbines and power time-evolution characteristics. Based on real data collected from a multi-turbine wind farm, the proposed model achieves the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0455 and 0.0864, clearly exceeding the accuracy of popular benchmark models like TimeMixer and ETSformer. Relative to the best-performing baseline, MAE decreases by approximately 4.8%. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of ultra-short-term wind power forecasting under complex wind conditions, providing reliable support for grid scheduling decisions in high-proportion wind power integration scenarios.</jats:p>
title: DSTC-Net: A Physics-Informed Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Coupling Network for Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting
